name: Sequence Poker
description: Poker variant where hands include sequences. Combines poker with sequence-building mechanics.
deck: Standard 52-card French deck; four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades), thirteen ranks per suit (Ace through King). Used for five-card hands and standard poker hand rankings including straights.

history.origins: Sequence Poker is documented as a poker variant focused on sequence-building hand value; straights (sequences) are central to hand ranking.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card French deck; four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades), thirteen ranks per suit (Ace through King). Used for five-card hands and standard poker hand rankings including straights.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt five cards one at a time, face down. No further cards are dealt during the hand.

rules.objective: Win by having the best five-card hand at showdown. Hand values use standard poker rankings with sequences (straights) counting in hand evaluation.
rules.gameplay: Poker variant where hands include sequences. Each player receives five cards. After the deal, hands are compared at showdown; the highest hand wins. No betting rounds in the basic form.
keyRules: Standard 52-card deck, five cards per player.
Hands ranked by standard poker order: straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair, high card.
Sequence (straight) is five consecutive ranks; A-2-3-4-5 (wheel) and 10-J-Q-K-A (broadway) are valid straights.

strategy.basic: Hold cards that can form straights or high pairs; discard weak high cards that block sequences.
strategy.intermediate: Track which ranks have been dealt to estimate opponents' straight potential; prefer connected cards over disconnected high cards.
strategy.advanced: Balance bluffing a strong sequence with actually building one; late position can represent straights more effectively.
tips: A-2-3-4-5 (wheel) and 10-J-Q-K-A (broadway) are the two ace-high straights; both count in standard poker order.
In a no-betting variant, hand selection is key; aim for hands that make straights or strong pairs.

scoring.winCondition: Highest five-card hand at showdown wins. Standard poker rankings: straight flush down to high card.
